adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's national 'LGBTQ rights in Turkey' page documents the framework a trans visitor to Sivas stands under: homosexuality has been decriminalised since the 1858 Ottoman penal code, transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988 (via gender-reassignment surgery, medical examination and court permission), but there is no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity, same-sex marriage and civil unions are not recognised, and LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military. Since 2015, authorities have banned Pride events in Istanbul and other cities in most years, with police using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants who defied the bans; on 14 June 2019 the Istanbul, İzmir and Antalya prides were each banned by their cities' governors. When the 12th judicial reform package passed in 2026, provisions discriminating against LGBTQ people were removed from the bill, leaving only symbolic same-sex weddings with no legal marital status, and in early 2026 Turkish media reported the government was considering legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex' (ultimately not included in that package); in ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking Turkey placed 47th of 49 countries assessed. The page documents no Sivas-specific measure, incident or institution; it supports this provincial record's national-framework claims, which per the audited sources are the only documented basis.

adds.title: Human rights in Türkiye - Amnesty International (Report 2025/26)
adds.summary: Amnesty International's Türkiye country report (Report 2025/26) records the national enforcement climate a visitor to Sivas stands under: in June 2025 authorities issued blanket bans against the LGBTI and Trans pride marches in Istanbul, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful use of force, and over 90 people were arbitrarily detained; three activists were remanded in prison on 29 June 2025 for violating Law No. 2911 and released on 8 August pending trial, while prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end. In December 2025 an İzmir court ordered the dissolution of the Young LGBTI+ Association, ruling it had shared 'obscene' images on social media that were incompatible with 'society's moral values' and could 'encourage or promote' LGBTI identities. The report also records that three draft law packages made public in 2025 - criminalising any expression of LGBTI identities and consensual same-sex relations and making legal gender recognition nearly impossible - were ultimately not submitted to parliament. No Sivas-specific incident is documented in the report; this is the province-level applicable national framework (blanket bans plus case-by-case prosecutions under the same Law No. 2911) that reaches provincial authorities in Sivas as it does across Turkey.
